jobs.title: Director of Solution Architecture
jobs.description:
At PwC Canada, we're transforming the way we work—and the way our people and clients experience technology. Our Products & Technology team builds the digital products, enterprise applications, and AI-enabled platforms that power the firm and shape the future of professional services. We're a community of solvers combining technology, data, and human ingenuity to deliver sustained outcomes that matter. We're looking for a Director of Solution Architecture to lead our established team of Senior Solution Architects—a technically deep, business-savvy leader who can set direction, grow and develop talent, and partner with senior leaders across the firm to turn ambitious ideas into reality. Reporting to the Architecture and Development Leader, you will lead PwC Canada's Solution Architecture practice within Products & Technology. You will take ownership of our established team of Senior Solution Architects, elevate their performance, and grow the team's capabilities as our technology ambitions expand. The team designs AI-enabled products, enterprise applications, and platforms used across the firm's lines of service, ensuring our solutions are secure, scalable, resilient, aligned with enterprise architecture standards—and deliver real business value. This is a hands-on architecture leadership role. While your focus is on design and technical direction rather than execution, you'll be expected to understand the technology from the inside. You'll go deep into architecture diagrams, integration designs, data flows, platform configurations, and the realities of how solutions are implemented, engaging with technical trade-offs at a practitioner level. Your credibility with the team and with stakeholders will come from genuine technical depth and a willingness to go hands-on with architecture and implementation details when the situation calls for it, not from high-level concepts alone. Equally, this role operates at the intersection of business and technology. You'll be a trusted advisor to business stakeholders and organizational leaders, translating complex challenges into clear technology solutions, influencing strategic direction, and communicating in terms that resonate with executives. You'll also help shape how PwC Canada adopts emerging technologies, including generative and agentic AI.

The Opportunity

As a Director of Solution Architecture, unlock your potential and embrace the chance to drive meaningful outcomes that’ll elevate your career. Your role will include, but isn’t limited to:

Provide architecture oversight for digital products, enterprise applications, and AI-enabled solutions from ideation through production
Lead solution design decisions, balancing reusable platform components with business-specific needs
Guide the architecture of enterprise applications—including SaaS platforms, ERP, CRM, HR, finance, and collaboration systems—ensuring effective integration, extensibility, and alignment with our broader technology ecosystem
Go hands-on with architecture and technical implementation details when needed—working through complex integration patterns, data flows, platform configurations, or design problems alongside the team
Advise on the adoption of emerging technologies, including generative and agentic AI
Manage, coach, and mentor an established team of talented Senior Solution Architects, elevating performance and fostering a culture of technical excellence and continuous learning
Grow the team's capabilities over time—identifying skill gaps, developing talent from within, and recruiting new members as the practice expands
Evolve team structure and define new roles as the practice grows and technology priorities shift
Partner with Enterprise Architecture, Data, Security, and Risk teams to ensure solutions align with firm standards
Participate in architecture review boards and technology governance forums, advising on governance requirements, risk assessments, and policy exceptions
Contribute to PwC's broader architecture community—locally and across the global PwC network

What You’ll Bring

Your skills, knowledge, and experiences are what set you apart. Here’s what we look for:

Experience in technology roles, including significant time in solution or enterprise architecture, with extensive experience designing and delivering solutions within large, complex organizations
Proven experience leading, developing, and growing a team of Senior Solution Architects—setting technical direction, elevating performance, and fostering a high-performance culture, including in an Agile/DevOps environment
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science or Computer Engineering
Azure Cloud Platform certifications (Solutions Architect or Developer) preferred; TOGAF certification
Strong technical depth as an architect—able to engage with the technology from the inside, work through implementation-level details, and go hands-on with architecture and design when the situation requires it
Enterprise application architecture, including SaaS and COTS platforms (ERP, CRM, HCM, finance, collaboration, workflow), integration patterns (APIs, iPaaS, event-driven), and configuration vs. customization trade-offs
Cloud-native architectures on Azure (AWS/GCP nice to have), including containerization and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes) and DevOps practices such as CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure-as-code
Generative AI and agentic AI solution design, including LLM integration, RAG patterns, and responsible AI practices
Enterprise software architecture and design patterns, including service-oriented, event-driven, and microservices architectures; data architecture and persistence strategies (RDBMS, NoSQL); and Big Data, analytics, and AI/ML architecture
Security-by-design, privacy, and compliance considerations, plus vendor and product evaluation, including RFP processes, proof-of-concepts, and total-cost-of-ownership analysis
Demonstrated experience advising and partnering with senior business leaders on technology strategy and investment decisions; experience in professional services or consulting environments is an asset
This role does not require professional engineering licensure and is not classified as a formal engineering position under provincial regulatory definitions. While individuals with a P.Eng designation are welcome to apply, the responsibilities of this role do not involve the practice of professional engineering as defined by applicable legislation.

This position ensures continuity and upholds our standards of excellence following the departure of a valued team member.

The salary range for this position is $196,000 - $246,000. The posted salary range represents the expected hiring range for PwC locations in major city centres. Given our national recruiting approach, ranges may vary for positions in other locations. At PwC Canada, base salary is determined by your skills, experience, qualifications and work location. In addition to base salary, eligible employees may have opportunities to participate in variable incentive pay programs which are designed to reward individual and firm-wide achievements. We are committed to offering competitive compensation and adhere to all relevant pay transparency legislation. During the hiring process, our Talent Acquisition team will provide details about our comprehensive total rewards package.

Why you’ll love PwC

We’re inspiring and empowering our people to change the world. Powered by the latest technology, you’ll be a part of diverse teams helping public and private clients build trust and deliver sustained outcomes. This meaningful work, and our continuous development environment, will take your career to the next level. We reward your impact, and support your wellbeing, through a competitive compensation package, inclusive benefits and flexibility programs that will help you thrive in work and life. Learn more about our Application Process and Total Rewards Package at: https://jobs-ca.pwc.com/ca/en/life-at-pwc

jobs.description:
About The Lacroix Medical Group

A leader in private medicine in Quebec, the Lacroix Medical Group comprises three rapidly growing divisions:

Medical Clinics
Operating Rooms
Biomedical Laboratory

The organization has experienced strong and sustained growth since its founding in 2009 and currently employs nearly 350 people. As part of its strategic plan, the Group aims to accelerate its national and international development.

OUR MISSION

To be the benchmark in private healthcare.

OUR VALUES

Passion | Respect | Integrity | Commitment | Innovation.

The Mandate

In a context of sustained growth and transformation of its activities, Lacroix Medical Group is seeking a Director of Information Technology who will actively contribute to the organization's technological evolution.

Reporting directly to the President and CEO, the Director of IT plays a strategic role across the entire network. They are responsible for defining, structuring, and developing the IT function to effectively support the organization's operations, growth, and ambitions.

They provide leadership for technology strategy, infrastructure, business systems, cybersecurity, data governance, digital transformation, and artificial intelligence.

He is also responsible for the performance of his team and the organization's technology partner ecosystem. This role is for an experienced, business-oriented, and results-driven IT leader who can combine strategic vision with excellent execution. Your Key Responsibilities IT Strategy and Governance: Define and deploy the IT vision and master plan in line with the strategic, operational, and financial priorities of Groupe médical Lacroix. Advise senior management on investments, risks, and key technological choices.

Performance and Business Continuity

Ensure the performance, robustness, and high availability of the infrastructure and technology platforms essential to the network's medical and administrative activities, including ERP, CRM, DME, LIS, SaaS, and cloud environments.

Digital Transformation, Data, and Artificial Intelligence

Identify and prioritize initiatives to transform the organization through technology, data valorization, automation, and artificial intelligence. Lead major technology projects and ensure their effective integration into operations.

Cybersecurity and Risk Management

Maintain high standards in cybersecurity, information protection, redundancy, and business continuity in an environment where system availability and the protection of medical data are critical.

Leadership and Organizational Performance

Lead and develop a competent, autonomous, and accountable IT team. Establish clear objectives and performance indicators, ensure rigorous budget management, and optimize the contribution of suppliers, consultants, and technology partners.

An Executive Role Close to Operations

At Lacroix Medical Group, technology must meet the realities on the ground.

The IT Director will therefore need to maintain close contact with the various business units and network teams to understand their needs, anticipate challenges, and ensure that technological solutions contribute concretely to operational performance and service quality.

The position consequently requires excellent mobility. The successful candidate will be required to travel regularly throughout the Lacroix network in Quebec to meet with teams, support projects, and remain connected to the operational realities of the various facilities.

This on-the-ground presence is an essential component of the role and not an occasional responsibility.

The mandate expressly includes regular visits to service points.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for an experienced manager with a strong business acumen and excellent technological expertise, recognized for their leadership, judgment, and ability to drive organizational growth.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

A bachelor's degree in computer engineering, computer science, or a related field;
15 to 20 years of experience in information technology, including a minimum of 5 years in a management role;
Mastery of software architecture and project management;
A solid understanding of multi-site and cloud infrastructures;
Good knowledge of SaaS environments and major business platforms: ERP, CRM, financial systems, telephony, Microsoft 365, and others;
A thorough understanding of the issues cybersecurity, data governance and valorization, and artificial intelligence;
Proven experience in team management and development;
Recognized leadership in transformation and change management;
Ability to prioritize, make decisions, and manage effectively in a complex and evolving environment;
Excellent business acumen and the ability to communicate technological issues to senior management;
Fluency in French and English, both written and spoken;
A valid driver's license, a vehicle, and significant availability for regular travel throughout the network.

The Leader Profile We Are Looking For

Beyond technological expertise, we are looking for someone who stands out for their ability to mobilize, structure, and deliver.

A positive and committed leader with a strong sense of Accountability, the ability to build high-performing teams, manage rigorously, challenge the status quo, and transform technological challenges into concrete solutions for the business. The IT Director must be equally comfortable discussing strategy with senior management and understanding the challenges faced by teams in the field. Conditions and Compensation Lacroix Medical Group offers a competitive total compensation package including: Annual salary of $140,000 to $175,000, depending on experience and expertise; 4 weeks of vacation and 4 paid personal days; RRSP+ program with employer contribution; Cell phone allowance; Lacroix Health Credit; and an annual Lacroix gift card. This benefit can be combined with other benefits for personalized medical services.

Business travel expense account for trips outside your usual work area

Join a growing network and become a key player in the future of private medicine in Quebec.

Apply now and make a real difference.

Overview

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the Vice President, Enterprise Services brings an organization-wide perspective to strategy, performance, technology, people and enterprise risk.
This position provides executive leadership and strategic direction for Enterprise Services and is integral to WorkplaceNL’s modernization agenda, working in partnership with those leading transformation initiatives to ensure improvements are effectively integrated into ongoing operations. Your mandate extends beyond leading your portfolio: you will work across organizational boundaries, navigate competing needs and build support for changes that strengthen services and organizational performance.

You will also lead the continued development of WorkplaceNL’s Enterprise Risk Management Framework and report to the Board’s Governance Committee.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Strategy and planning:
Working with the Executive Team and senior leaders to translate long-term priorities into evidence-based, multi-year plans with clear accountabilities and measurable outcomes.

Technology and information management:

IMMEDIATE INTERIM OPPORTUNITY

Interim Chief Information Officer

Reports to: President

Location: Greater Toronto Area, Ontario

Duration: 6-12 Months

Hybrid working

Our client, a large and complex Ontario post-secondary institution, is seeking an accomplished Interim Chief Information Officer
to provide leadership through an important period of transition, modernization and organizational evolution.

This is an exciting opportunity for a seasoned technology executive who can combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution
.

The organization recognizes that technology has the potential to play a much greater role in how it operates, how decisions are made, how services are delivered and how students experience the institution. The Interim CIO will be asked not simply to manage the existing technology environment, but to challenge conventional thinking about how technology is deployed and where it can fundamentally improve the operating model.

Leading a team of more than 100 technology professionals, the successful executive will initially provide stability, clarity and leadership through transition. Beyond this, they will help establish the priorities, capabilities, operating model and roadmap required for the next stage of the organization's technology journey.

This is therefore a mandate for a builder, modernizer and objective disruptor
, someone able to respect what is working while constructively challenging what could be done differently.

The Mandate

The Interim CIO will provide overall leadership to the technology function while working closely with the organization's senior leadership team to determine how technology can better enable its academic, student and operational priorities.

A central component of the mandate will be assessing the technology operating model
and identifying opportunities to improve effectiveness, service, scalability and value.
The Interim CIO will be expected to create alignment between technology strategy and organizational strategy, while maintaining a bias toward execution and measurable outcomes.

Key priorities will include:

Technology Strategy & Operating Model

Assess the current technology environment, capabilities, organizational structure and priorities and establish a clear roadmap for the next phase of modernization.
Challenge existing assumptions around how technology services are organized, delivered and supported.
Identify opportunities to simplify processes, reduce complexity, improve scalability and improve the value generated from technology investment
.
Evaluate the appropriate balance between internal capabilities, external partnerships, managed services and selective outsourcing.
Introduce stronger prioritization and governance disciplines to ensure technology resources are focused on the areas of greatest institutional impact.
Translate technology strategy into a practical execution agenda with clear accountabilities and outcomes.

Leadership Through Change

The Interim CIO will inherit a substantial team of 100+ technology professionals
and will need to quickly establish credibility and provide visible, confident leadership.

The organization operates within a unionized environment. Accordingly, the executive must understand how to lead meaningful organizational and operational change while respecting collective agreements, established processes and employee relationships.

The successful individual will:

Provide stability and clarity during transition.
Assess organizational capability, structure and accountabilities.
Coach and develop technology leaders.
Build stronger accountability for results.
Engage employees in the modernization journey.
Create a strong service and performance culture.
Navigate change thoughtfully within a complex unionized environment
.
Maintain momentum while making difficult decisions where required.

ERP Optimization & Enterprise Platforms

An important priority will be continuing to optimize the organization's ERP and broader enterprise technology environment.

The Interim CIO will:

Assess the current ERP implementation and identify opportunities to increase adoption, functionality and organizational value.
Address process, integration, data and operating-model issues that may inhibit the organization from realizing the full value of its enterprise platforms.
Challenge the proliferation of unnecessary processes, applications and workarounds where these create complexity.
Ensure technology modernization is accompanied by process modernization rather than simply automating existing ways of working
.
Strengthen the connection between enterprise systems, organizational processes and user experience.

Cybersecurity, Risk & Resilience

Cybersecurity will be a significant part of the mandate.

The Interim CIO will assess and evolve the organization's cybersecurity posture, governance and protocols, ensuring they remain appropriate for a large, complex and highly distributed post-secondary environment.

The executive will work to strengthen areas including security governance, accountability, organizational awareness and operational resilience, while ensuring cybersecurity is understood as an enterprise risk rather than simply an IT responsibility
.

The successful candidate will balance increasingly sophisticated security requirements with the accessibility, flexibility and innovation expected within a modern educational institution.

Cloud & Technology Modernization

The organization has begun elements of its cloud journey, but further opportunity remains to modernize its technology architecture and operating environment.

The Interim CIO will assess where further migration and modernization create genuine operational, financial, resilience or user-experience benefits.

They will bring an objective perspective regarding cloud strategy, legacy environments, technical debt, architecture and application rationalization
, ensuring modernization is driven by institutional value rather than technology for technology's sake.

Data Governance, Analytics & Decision Support

Data represents a significant opportunity for the organization.

The Interim CIO will help establish stronger data governance, ownership, quality and analytics capabilities
, enabling leaders across the institution to make better and faster decisions based on reliable information.

The mandate will include helping the organization move beyond reporting toward a culture where trusted data and actionable insights routinely inform operational, financial, academic and student-focused decision-making.

This will require both technology leadership and the ability to address the governance, accountability and behavioural changes necessary to establish a more mature data culture.

Artificial Intelligence

The organization recognizes the potentially significant role AI could play in both its operating model and the broader evolution of post-secondary education.

The Interim CIO will help leadership distinguish between experimentation and sustainable enterprise adoption, identifying practical opportunities where AI, automation and emerging technologies can improve productivity, decision-making and service delivery
.

Equally important will be establishing appropriate governance around the adoption of these technologies, including cybersecurity, privacy, data, risk and responsible use.

The successful executive will bring curiosity and ambition around AI while maintaining the pragmatic judgment required to translate emerging technology into sustainable institutional value.

The Evolving Student Experience

Technology is increasingly integral to the complete student journey.

How students learn, interact with faculty, access services, consume information and engage with an institution continues to evolve.

The Interim CIO will work across the organization to consider how technology can help create a simpler, more integrated, personalized and contemporary student experience
.

The opportunity extends beyond classroom technology. It is about understanding how technology can differentiate the institution and reduce friction across the entire student journey.

Service Culture

A key leadership priority will be continuing to evolve the technology function toward a highly responsive, accountable and customer-focused service organization.

The Interim CIO will establish clear expectations around service delivery, ownership, responsiveness and partnership with internal stakeholders.

Technology should increasingly be viewed as an enabler and partner to the organization
, rather than simply a provider of systems and infrastructure.

The Ideal Interim Executive

The successful candidate will be an accomplished CIO or senior enterprise technology executive
who has led a sizeable, complex technology function through significant modernization and organizational change.

They will bring experience across a combination of:

Enterprise technology strategy and execution.
Leadership of large, multidisciplinary technology teams.
Technology operating-model transformation.
ERP and enterprise application optimization.
Cloud migration and modernization.
Cybersecurity, risk and technology governance.
Data governance, analytics and information management.
AI, automation and emerging technologies.
Process optimization and organizational simplification.
Managed services, strategic sourcing and outsourcing.
Vendor and commercial management.
Digital/customer experience transformation.
Leadership in a unionized environment.
Organizational change and talent development.

Experience within higher education or the broader public sector
would be highly relevant, although the organization will also be interested in executives from other large, complex and regulated environments who can bring fresh thinking and transferable experience.

Leadership Style

This mandate requires more than technical credibility.

The ideal executive will be pragmatic, curious, commercially minded and comfortable challenging the status quo
. They will know when to listen and preserve institutional knowledge, but equally when to push the organization toward a different approach.

They will be capable of moving comfortably between the boardroom and the technology organization, translating complex technology issues into clear discussions about risk, cost, service, productivity and organizational outcomes
.

Most importantly, this individual will be an objective disruptor with strong execution discipline
.
They will leave the organization not simply with better technology, but with a stronger technology function, clearer priorities, improved governance, better use of data, enhanced cybersecurity and a pragmatic roadmap for how technology can enable the institution's future operating model.

The attraction of the assignment

For an experienced CIO, this is a rare opportunity to have meaningful impact in a relatively short period.

The mandate combines people leadership, technology modernization, ERP optimization, cyber, cloud, data and analytics, AI, operating-model transformation and student experience
within one of the most rapidly changing sectors in Canada.

The successful interim will have the platform to challenge existing thinking, accelerate decisions and help redefine the role technology plays across the institution.

This is not a mandate to simply keep the lights on. It is an opportunity to shape what technology leadership, capability and service should look like for the organization's next chapter.

About The Role

Reporting to the Interim CEO, Performance & N9NE, the Director, Inventory Planning & Replenishment
is responsible for improving product availability and inventory health by ensuring the right approved products are available in the right quantities and locations, at the right time. The Director builds reliable forecasting and replenishment processes and drives effective use of Streamline demand-planning software while balancing customer service and inventory investment.
The Director leads planning and replenishment for Performance and N9NE and develops common planning methods with Source. This is a hands-on leadership role: it combines operating accountability, team development and planning-process improvement with strong cross-functional coordination across Customer Service, Purchasing, Warehousing and Logistics. The Director partners with Source's planning lead on common methods and Streamline adoption; Source retains its planning and replenishment execution and existing reporting structure.
The immediate priorities are reliable replenishment, effective use of Streamline and stronger internal capability.

Main Responsibilities

Forecasting

•Build rolling demand and supply plans from sales history, commercial input, product plans and supplier constraints. Test commercial assumptions and translate agreed demand into inventory requirements.
•Measure forecast error and bias at relevant replenishment horizons. Separate underlying demand, projects and growth assumptions; reconcile intercompany demand to avoid double-counting.
•Lead the demand-planning review with Sales and Product as part of the monthly planning cycle, reviewing and adjusting forecasts for trends, projects, promotions and new items.
Replenishment and inventory health
•Own Performance/N9NE replenishment plans and decisions within delegated limits: which approved items to buy or transfer, how much, when and where. Work with Purchasing and Operations to ensure approved replenishment plans are executed and exceptions are resolved.
•Maintain planning parameters, including lead times, safety stock, service targets, minimum/maximum levels, order cycles and supplier minimum order quantities (MOQs).
•Manage shortage, excess, slow-moving and obsolete inventory exposure. Recommend recovery, transfer and run-out actions; escalate material cash commitments, write-offs and service trade-offs.
•Use ABC/XYZ segmentation to set differentiated service levels, planning parameters and inventory policies.

Demand planning / Streamline ownership

•Establish the planning rules and logic for Streamline, including forecasting and replenishment parameters, workflow design, testing, user training and adoption. Maintain internal ownership after go-live.
•Partner with Source on its planning workflows and adoption. Work with IT, the implementation provider and named data owners on technical delivery, data validation and issue resolution.
•Manage planning milestones and issues, validate licence needs against actual workflows and test replenishment outputs. Embed routine planning in Streamline, with documented exceptions and overrides.

Review discipline and common methods

•Run weekly replenishment reviews and a practical monthly demand, supply and inventory review for Performance/N9NE. Present service, inventory and cash trade-offs for business-leader decisions.
•Lead agreed KPI definitions, planning controls and Streamline methods with Source. Sequence improvements against the agreed work plan and available capacity.

Inventory network planning

•Set and manage inventory-transfer rules within approved service and inventory targets; agree transfer frequency with Operations, balancing availability, inventory investment and freight cost.
•Evaluate hub-and-spoke replenishment with Operations and implement the agreed inventory-planning approach.
•Define stocked versus non-stocked item strategy by location.

Product lifecycle inventory planning

•Translate supplier lead times, minimum orders, production availability, container constraints and warehouse capacity into inventory plans. Purchasing and Operations retain supplier-order follow-up and physical execution.
•Develop first-buy, launch-stock, phased-receipt and run-out plans with Product and commercial teams. Quantify inventory exposure before commitments; Product/Sourcing retains product and supplier decisions.

People, knowledge and reporting

•Develop assigned planners, assess capacity and establish documented workflows and backup coverage. Capture critical operating knowledge and strengthen the team’s independence.
•Publish an inventory and availability scorecard with root causes, actions and owners. Work with Finance to validate benefits and with data owners to resolve planning-data issues.

Knowledge and Experience

•Typically, 8–12+ years of relevant demand, inventory or replenishment planning experience, including people leadership and cross-functional change.
•Proven improvement in availability and inventory health in multi-location distribution, imported finished goods, furniture, building products or a comparable inventory-intensive business.
•Hands-on delivery of planning-platform implementation or adoption. Streamline experience is an asset; broader planning and implementation capability is essential.
•Strong command of forecasting, safety stock, supplier lead times, service targets, order constraints, multi-location replenishment, working-capital trade-offs, ERP data and analytical tools.
•Experience establishing practical demand/supply reviews, developing planners and working constructively with Sales, Product, Purchasing, Operations and Finance.
•Relevant degree or equivalent experience; relevant planning or supply-chain certification is an asset. Ability to work from Burnaby and travel to Canadian and U.S. operating locations as required.
•A practical, hands-on builder who combines analytical depth with commercial judgement. The Director respects existing expertise, challenges assumptions constructively, explains decisions clearly and develops capability that stays with the organisation.

About The Role

Reporting to the Interim CEO, Performance & N9NE, the Director, Inventory Planning & Replenishment
is responsible for improving product availability and inventory health by ensuring the right approved products are available in the right quantities and locations, at the right time. The Director builds reliable forecasting and replenishment processes and drives effective use of Streamline demand-planning software while balancing customer service and inventory investment.
The Director leads planning and replenishment for Performance and N9NE and develops common planning methods with Source. This is a hands-on leadership role: it combines operating accountability, team development and planning-process improvement with strong cross-functional coordination across Customer Service, Purchasing, Warehousing and Logistics. The Director partners with Source's planning lead on common methods and Streamline adoption; Source retains its planning and replenishment execution and existing reporting structure.
The immediate priorities are reliable replenishment, effective use of Streamline and stronger internal capability.

Main Responsibilities

Forecasting

•Build rolling demand and supply plans from sales history, commercial input, product plans and supplier constraints. Test commercial assumptions and translate agreed demand into inventory requirements.
•Measure forecast error and bias at relevant replenishment horizons. Separate underlying demand, projects and growth assumptions; reconcile intercompany demand to avoid double-counting.
•Lead the demand-planning review with Sales and Product as part of the monthly planning cycle, reviewing and adjusting forecasts for trends, projects, promotions and new items.
Replenishment and inventory health
•Own Performance/N9NE replenishment plans and decisions within delegated limits: which approved items to buy or transfer, how much, when and where. Work with Purchasing and Operations to ensure approved replenishment plans are executed and exceptions are resolved.
•Maintain planning parameters, including lead times, safety stock, service targets, minimum/maximum levels, order cycles and supplier minimum order quantities (MOQs).
•Manage shortage, excess, slow-moving and obsolete inventory exposure. Recommend recovery, transfer and run-out actions; escalate material cash commitments, write-offs and service trade-offs.
•Use ABC/XYZ segmentation to set differentiated service levels, planning parameters and inventory policies.

Demand planning / Streamline ownership

•Establish the planning rules and logic for Streamline, including forecasting and replenishment parameters, workflow design, testing, user training and adoption. Maintain internal ownership after go-live.
•Partner with Source on its planning workflows and adoption. Work with IT, the implementation provider and named data owners on technical delivery, data validation and issue resolution.
•Manage planning milestones and issues, validate licence needs against actual workflows and test replenishment outputs. Embed routine planning in Streamline, with documented exceptions and overrides.

Review discipline and common methods

•Run weekly replenishment reviews and a practical monthly demand, supply and inventory review for Performance/N9NE. Present service, inventory and cash trade-offs for business-leader decisions.
•Lead agreed KPI definitions, planning controls and Streamline methods with Source. Sequence improvements against the agreed work plan and available capacity.

Inventory network planning

•Set and manage inventory-transfer rules within approved service and inventory targets; agree transfer frequency with Operations, balancing availability, inventory investment and freight cost.
•Evaluate hub-and-spoke replenishment with Operations and implement the agreed inventory-planning approach.
•Define stocked versus non-stocked item strategy by location.

Product lifecycle inventory planning

•Translate supplier lead times, minimum orders, production availability, container constraints and warehouse capacity into inventory plans. Purchasing and Operations retain supplier-order follow-up and physical execution.
•Develop first-buy, launch-stock, phased-receipt and run-out plans with Product and commercial teams. Quantify inventory exposure before commitments; Product/Sourcing retains product and supplier decisions.

People, knowledge and reporting

•Develop assigned planners, assess capacity and establish documented workflows and backup coverage. Capture critical operating knowledge and strengthen the team’s independence.
•Publish an inventory and availability scorecard with root causes, actions and owners. Work with Finance to validate benefits and with data owners to resolve planning-data issues.

Knowledge and Experience

•Typically, 8–12+ years of relevant demand, inventory or replenishment planning experience, including people leadership and cross-functional change.
•Proven improvement in availability and inventory health in multi-location distribution, imported finished goods, furniture, building products or a comparable inventory-intensive business.
•Hands-on delivery of planning-platform implementation or adoption. Streamline experience is an asset; broader planning and implementation capability is essential.
•Strong command of forecasting, safety stock, supplier lead times, service targets, order constraints, multi-location replenishment, working-capital trade-offs, ERP data and analytical tools.
•Experience establishing practical demand/supply reviews, developing planners and working constructively with Sales, Product, Purchasing, Operations and Finance.
•Relevant degree or equivalent experience; relevant planning or supply-chain certification is an asset. Ability to work from Burnaby and travel to Canadian and U.S. operating locations as required.
•A practical, hands-on builder who combines analytical depth with commercial judgement. The Director respects existing expertise, challenges assumptions constructively, explains decisions clearly and develops capability that stays with the organisation.
